messages:
oliver: Customer 'FinServe' on Private (eu-central) opened a support ticket: seeing p95 ~600ms, spikes to 1.2s. They provided a trace that suggests traffic is egressing to our us-west front instead of eu-central. Can we triage?

samir: can you share a sample request id, SNAT ip, and any client-side traceroute/curl output so we can validate headers and path?

oliver: sample req: req_fins_0421, client egress ip: 35.195.78.162

oliver: traceroute (from customer's bastion):
traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.58.23.12), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.0.1 0.6 ms 0.5 ms 0.5 ms
 2 100.64.1.1 1.3 ms 1.0 ms 1.1 ms
 3 10.200.0.5 3.5 ms 3.2 ms 3.4 ms
 4 52.58.23.12 94.8 ms 95.2 ms 95.0 ms

jess: next-hop looks like one of our us-west front IPs (52.58.23.12). li can you check the peering/route selection for that customer prefix?

li: looking at the hub routes: the customer's SNAT prefix 35.195.78.0/24 is being learned with next-hop pointing at our us-west transit (bgp-origin: usw-transit-1). There's an older route-map that defaults to prefer-us-west when the subnet lacks a region-preference tag.

samir: can you paste the route-map rules? wondering if tag propagation failed during the infra rollout.

li: route-map egress-pref permit 10
 set community 65000:200 ; # prefer-us-west
route-map egress-pref permit 20
 set community 65000:100 ; # prefer-eu

li: customer subnets are missing the "region-preference" tag. Looks like Terraform drift (these subnets pre-date tagging enforcement). Without the tag, rule 10 wins and traffic heads to us-west.

oliver: customer insists they didn't change anything. Their private control plane shows eu-central. They want a non-disruptive fix (no tenant restart).

samir: short-term: inject a host route (/32) for the SNAT ip pointing at eu-transit, or temporarily adjust the route-map to check control-plane metadata before the tag fallback. I'll prep a canary-safe static route that doesn't withdraw existing BGP for now.

deploy-bot: change started: egress-hotfix -> staging -> canary

jess: before we touch routing, ask customer to run a curl with X-Request-Id so we can verify which front served it in our ingress logs.

oliver: customer ran: curl -sI -H "X-Request-Id: req_fins_0421" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
HTTP/2 200
x-request-id: req_fins_0421
x-region: us-west-2

samir: x-region header from our front confirms the request landed on a us-west front. Good repro.

li: injecting static /32 for 35.195.78.162 -> next-hop eu-transit-2 into the hub (no BGP withdraw). Will push in 30s, monitor for path churn.

jess: monitoring: small route-change event, connection churn negligible. Keep watching latency and errors.

oliver: customer reports immediate improvement: p95 down to ~45ms after route applied. They see eu-front serving the next 200 calls.

samir: draft root-cause: Terraform drift removed region-preference tag on subnets. Route-map fallback preferred us-west. Mitigation: static host route for SNAT IP + route-map reordering. Permanent fixes: make control-plane metadata authoritative in routing logic (P1), add tag-sync job to detect drift (P2), e2e check to validate tenant egress affinity after infra changes (P2).

li: I'll commit the route-map reorder that checks control-plane metadata first and add a changelog entry linking the commit. Plan to rotate the temporary static routes out once route-map is live.

deploy-bot: egress-hotfix -> prod canary -> success

samir: Post-incident checklist for ops doc:
- Detection: customer latency spike + trace suggested wrong front
- Validation: curl + x-request-id confirmed us-west front served traffic
- Cause: missing region-preference tag -> route-map fallback chose us-west
- Short-term mitigation: static /32 to eu-transit (non-disruptive)
- Long-term: control-plane precedence in route logic, tag-sync, tenant e2e tests

jess: I'll draft the postmortem for the customer, include timeline and remediation plan. @oliver please confirm customer consent for sharing traces.

oliver: customer consent received, shared trace and traceroute. Closing with customer happy. Thanks all :raised_hands:

audit-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-1187 | severity: low | owner: samir | tags: private-vpc, nat, routing, terraform-drift
